## 1. Purpose

This procedure describes the general operation, calibration, and
quality control framework for colorimetric water analysis using the
Hach DR3900 benchtop spectrophotometer and the Hach DR900 portable
colorimeter. The SOP is designed as a modular framework: Section 6
covers instrument operation common to all analyses, while the
**Method Registry** (Section 7) provides chemistry-specific parameters
for each analyte (reagent kit, Hach method number, wavelength, range,
reaction time, and interferences). New chemistries can be added to the
registry as the lab's needs evolve, without rewriting the core SOP
[@hach_dr3900; @hach_dr900; @apha2012].


## 2. Scope

- **Applies to:** Colorimetric determination of nutrients (phosphorus,
  nitrate, nitrite, ammonia), metals (iron, manganese, copper, zinc,
  lead, chromium), and other water quality parameters (silica,
  sulfate, chloride, hardness) in surface water, groundwater,
  wastewater, and aqueous extracts using Hach pre-packaged reagent
  kits and stored programs
- **Does not apply to:** Analyses requiring external standards and
  user-prepared calibration curves (use the DR3900 in manual wavelength
  mode with a separate SOP); soil KCl extracts analyzed for
  NO~3~^-^/NH~4~^+^ via ion chromatography or flow injection (see
  [SOP-L403](SOP-L403-nitrate-ammonium-kcl.qmd))
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 133 (DR3900); field sites
  (DR900)

| Role              | Responsibility                              |

| Lab PI            | Approve methods, review QC data             |
| Lab Manager       | Maintain instruments, stock reagent kits, track lot numbers and expiration dates |
| Trained Personnel | Run analyses per this SOP, record results   |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use    |


## 4. Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical:** Hach reagent powder pillows and liquid reagents contain
  a variety of chemicals depending on the method. Some contain acids
  (e.g., sulfuric acid in the TNT plus vials), heavy metal indicators
  (e.g., cadmium in older nitrate methods), or oxidizers. Always
  review the SDS for each reagent kit before first use.
- **Physical:** The DR3900 digestion reactor (DRB200) operates at
  105--150 C; burn risk from hot vials. Some methods require a
  digestion step.
- **Biological:** Water samples may contain pathogens; handle with
  gloves.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Nitrile gloves
- [ ] Safety glasses (required for all reagent handling and digestion steps)
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Heat-resistant gloves (when handling hot digestion vials)

### Emergency Procedures

For reagent splashes to skin or eyes, flush immediately with water for
at least 15 minutes. Consult the reagent SDS for specific first aid.
Refer to
[SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd).

## 6. Procedure -- Instrument Operation

### 6.1 DR3900 Startup and Program Selection

1. Turn on the DR3900 using the power switch on the back panel
2. Allow the instrument to complete its self-check (approximately 30
   seconds)
3. From the home screen, select **Stored Programs**
4. Search by program number (see Method Registry, Section 7) or by
   analyte name
5. Select the correct program. The display will show the method
   wavelength, sample cell type, and measurement units.

### 6.2 DR900 Startup and Program Selection

1. Press the power button on the DR900
2. Select **Stored Programs** from the menu
3. Enter the program number or scroll to the analyte name
4. The display will confirm the method, wavelength, and sample cell type

### 6.3 Zeroing the Instrument (Blank)

Every Hach method requires a blank (zero) reading before measuring
samples.

1. Prepare the blank according to the specific method instructions:
   most methods use DI water in a clean sample cell; some methods use
   a reagent blank (sample plus all reagents except the color-developing
   reagent).
2. Wipe the outside of the sample cell with a lint-free tissue. For
   1-inch round cells, apply a thin coat of silicone oil and wipe with
   the oiling cloth.
3. Insert the blank into the cell holder, aligning the orientation mark
   with the arrow on the instrument
4. Close the light shield and press **Zero**. The display should read
   0.000 mg/L (or the appropriate unit).

### 6.4 General Measurement Workflow

The following workflow applies to all Hach methods. Chemistry-specific
details (reagent addition, reaction time, interferences) are in the
Method Registry (Section 7).

1. Collect or pour the required sample volume into a clean sample cell
   (the volume is method-specific; see Section 7)
2. Add the reagent(s) per the method instructions (powder pillow, liquid
   dropper, or TNT plus vial; see Section 7)
3. Mix as directed (swirl, invert, shake) and start the timer for the
   specified reaction time
4. While waiting, prepare the blank (Section 6.3)
5. After the reaction time has elapsed (and before the maximum hold time
   expires), wipe and insert the sample cell
6. Press **Read**. Record the result, units, sample ID, date, time,
   and method number in the lab notebook.
7. If the reading exceeds the method range, dilute the sample with DI
   water, re-run, and multiply the result by the dilution factor

::: {.callout-important}
Always read the method-specific Hach procedure document (included in
each reagent kit box or available at
[hach.com/procedures](https://www.hach.com/resources/procedures))
before running a method for the first time. This SOP provides the
general framework; the Hach procedure document is the definitive
reference for reagent handling, timing, and interferences for each
chemistry.
:::

### 6.5 Using TNT Plus Vials (DR3900 Only)

Many newer Hach methods use pre-dosed TNT plus vials, which reduce
reagent handling and waste [@hach_dr3900]:

1. Select the appropriate stored program for the TNT method
2. Remove the cap from the TNT vial
3. Pipette the specified sample volume into the vial using the included
   or indicated pipette
4. Cap, invert to mix (number of inversions specified per method),
   and start the timer
5. After the reaction time, wipe the vial and insert into the DR3900
   using the appropriate adapter
6. Press **Zero** with the blank vial (included in the TNT kit), then
   read the sample

### 6.6 Using the DRB200 Reactor (Digestion Methods)

Some methods (total phosphorus, total nitrogen, COD) require a
high-temperature digestion step:

1. Preheat the DRB200 to the temperature specified by the method (e.g.,
   105 C for total phosphorus, 150 C for COD)
2. Add sample and reagents to the digestion vial per the method
   instructions
3. Cap tightly and place in the reactor
4. Digest for the specified time (typically 30 minutes to 2 hours)
5. Remove vials using heat-resistant gloves and allow to cool to room
   temperature (or cool in a rack as specified)
6. Proceed with the color-development step and read on the DR3900

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hot Vial Safety
Never open digestion vials while hot. Pressure can build during
digestion. Allow vials to cool to room temperature or to the
temperature specified by the method before opening or reading.
:::

### 7.4 Adding a New Method to the Registry

When the lab acquires a new Hach reagent kit or needs to analyze a new
parameter:

1. Obtain the Hach procedure document for the method (from the kit box
   or [hach.com](https://www.hach.com/resources/procedures))
2. Review the SDS for all reagents in the kit
3. Fill in a new row in the appropriate table above with all required
   fields
4. Run the method on at least 3 known standard concentrations spanning
   the method range to verify that the instrument's stored program
   produces results within +/- 10% of the standard value
5. Run DI water blanks to confirm zero reading
6. Change the status from *TBD* to **Active** once validation is
   complete
7. Record the validation data, date, and analyst in the QC log


## 8. Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

### 8.1 Every Analytical Session

- **Blank:** Run a DI water blank at the start of each session. The
  blank must read within the method's stated detection limit of zero.
- **Standard check:** Run one mid-range Hach standard at the start and
  end of each session. Acceptance: +/- 10% of the stated value.
- **Duplicates:** Analyze at least 10% of samples in duplicate.
  Acceptable RPD: less than 20% for concentrations above 5 times the
  detection limit.

### 8.2 Calibration Verification

The DR3900 and DR900 use factory-programmed calibration curves that do
not require user calibration under normal conditions [@hach_dr3900;
@hach_dr900]. However:

- Run a multi-point verification using Hach-supplied standards at least
  annually or when the instrument is serviced
- If a standard check deviates by more than 10%, clean the sample cell,
  re-zero, and re-read. If the problem persists, contact Hach technical
  support.
- *TBD -- establish a schedule for annual verification and record in
  the instrument log*

### 8.3 Reagent Management

- Record the lot number and expiration date of each reagent kit when
  opened
- Do not use expired reagents
- Store reagents per the kit instructions (most powder pillows at room
  temperature; some TNT kits require refrigeration)
- Keep an inventory and reorder when stock falls below one kit per
  active method


## 9. Data Recording and Calculations

### 9.1 Dilution Corrections

$$
C_{\text{original}} = C_{\text{measured}} \times DF
$$

where $DF$ is the dilution factor (e.g., 10 mL sample diluted to
100 mL total = $DF$ of 10).

### 9.2 Unit Conversions

| From                   | To                     | Multiply by |
|:-----------------------|:-----------------------|:------------|
| mg/L NO~3~-N           | mg/L NO~3~^-^          | 4.427       |
| mg/L NH~3~-N           | mg/L NH~4~^+^          | 1.288       |
| mg/L PO~4~-P           | mg/L PO~4~^3-^         | 3.066       |
| ug/L                   | mg/L                   | 0.001       |

```{r}
#| label: unit-conversions
#| echo: true

# Common Hach unit conversions
convert_n_no3 <- function(mg_L_NO3_N) mg_L_NO3_N * 4.427
convert_n_nh4 <- function(mg_L_NH3_N) mg_L_NH3_N * 1.288
convert_p_po4 <- function(mg_L_PO4_P) mg_L_PO4_P * 3.066

# Example
cat(sprintf("2.5 mg/L NO3-N = %.1f mg/L NO3\n", convert_n_no3(2.5)))
cat(sprintf("0.8 mg/L NH3-N = %.1f mg/L NH4+\n", convert_n_nh4(0.8)))
cat(sprintf("0.42 mg/L PO4-P = %.2f mg/L PO4\n", convert_p_po4(0.42)))
```


## 10. Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                        | Disposal Method                          |
|:----------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Used powder pillow wrappers       | Standard trash (non-hazardous)           |
| Used TNT vials (acid-containing)  | Labeled waste container; EH&S hazardous waste |
| Cadmium reduction reagent waste   | Heavy metal waste; EH&S hazardous waste  |
| Other reagent waste               | Consult SDS; collect in appropriate container |
| DI water rinses                   | Drain                                    |
| Sample waste (non-hazardous water)| Drain with copious water                 |

::: {.callout-important}
The cadmium reduction nitrate method (NitraVer 5) generates cadmium
waste, which is a regulated heavy metal. Collect all cadmium-containing
waste in a designated container and dispose through EH&S. Consider
switching to the cadmium-free chromotropic acid TNT method for routine
analyses.
:::

## 12. Training Record

Before performing Hach colorimetric analyses independently, personnel
must:

1. Read this SOP, [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd),
   and [SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd)
2. Review the SDS for the specific reagent kit(s) they will use
3. Read the Hach procedure document for the specific method(s) they
   will run
4. Observe a trained operator perform a complete analysis (blank,
   standard check, samples) on the DR3900 or DR900
5. Perform a supervised analysis with acceptable QC results (blank
   within detection limit, standard within 10%, duplicates within 20%
   RPD)
6. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager for each specific method


## Appendix A: DR3900 vs. DR900 Comparison {.appendix}

| Feature              | DR3900 (Benchtop)              | DR900 (Portable)               |
|:---------------------|:-------------------------------|:-------------------------------|
| Light source         | Tungsten and deuterium lamps   | LED array                      |
| Wavelength range     | 320--1100 nm (continuous)      | Discrete LED wavelengths       |
| Cell types           | 10 mm, 1-inch round, 16 mm TNT | 1-inch round                  |
| Stored programs      | 200+                           | 90+                            |
| User programs        | Yes                            | Limited                        |
| Power                | AC                             | 4 AA batteries                 |
| Best for             | Lab bench; full method library; TNT plus vials | Field screening; grab samples |
| Limitations          | Not portable                   | Fewer methods; no TNT vials; no UV wavelengths |

::: {.callout-note}
If a method is available on both instruments, use the DR3900 for
reportable data. The DR900 is best used for field screening and
preliminary results that will be confirmed on the benchtop instrument.
:::
